title: Stonecourse
status: core + cabinet in PR; iterations in PR; dossier is iteration 10
summary: The wall yard at the end of the Prismheart arcade row, where the dry-stone boundary is rebuilt every season. A seeded supply of cut stones comes off the cart in order; each one is set at a column and lands on the lowest course that holds it fully, no overhang allowed. A course with no gaps locks. A few stones may be skipped to the rubble. Every build is solvable by construction; the craft is leaving gaps that the stones still coming can fill. Deterministic per seed, bit-exact between the Python rules, the C++ core and the Unreal cabinet.

mechanics.name: Wall and supply
mechanics.text: A wall 7 / 8 / 9 cells wide and 4 / 5 / 6 courses high. 20 / 26 / 34 stones of width 1-3 are drawn in order. Setup redraws the supply (up to 50 times) until the mason's bounded search can finish the wall, so every build has an answer.

mechanics.name: Setting
mechanics.text: The next stone is set at a column: it occupies the lowest course whose cells there are empty, and every cell under it must be filled (the footing counts). Overhang, and a stone that would sit over an empty cell, are refused and cost nothing.

mechanics.name: Locking
mechanics.text: A course with no gaps locks (+10). Courses lock in any order the stones allow; a gap narrower than every stone still coming can never be filled, which is what the skips are for.

mechanics.name: Skips
mechanics.text: 3 skips per build send the next stone to the rubble. A stone that fits nowhere ends the build only when no skips are left.

mechanics.name: Finish and failure
mechanics.text: Every course locked finishes the wall: +2 per stone left in the supply, +3 per skip unused. The supply running out, or a stone that fits nowhere with no skips left, fails the build with the score so far.

mechanics.name: Mason (demo)
mechanics.text: A bounded exact search over (wall, supply index, skips): columns left to right for the next stone, then a skip; states pruned when the stone left is less than the empty cells; memoised; 20,000-node budget. Its first action is the pick; otherwise a gap-aware greedy (lowest course, no gap narrower than the smallest stone still coming, leftmost; skip when every placement leaves one). The mason finishes every seeded build; the greedy alone wins about 75 / 71 / 77 percent.

mechanics.name: Preview
mechanics.text: preview(action) gives the landing course and whether the course locks, without setting the stone; the native sweep proves it equals the real move. It draws the ghost stone, the lock ticks and the rests/locks line.

mechanics.name: Guide (option 1)
mechanics.text: Practice mode marks the mason's column in blue (or says it skips). In both modes the next stone is drawn as a ghost where it would land (red when it does not rest), and green ticks mark the columns that would lock a course.

mechanics.name: Saves
mechanics.text: Text save (shared DaedalusDesktopSaveText shape): difficulty, seed, index, wall rows, locked, skips, marker, score, over, won. Restore regenerates the supply from the seed and checks full support course by course, no more stone than the supply taken, locked = full courses, skips consistent with stones taken, and the flags; Python from_state applies the same checks and only accepts a stuck ending when the build is in fact stuck.

mechanics.name: Controls
mechanics.text: Left/Right (or stick) move the marker (the stone's left edge); A / J / Space set the stone; K / pad B skip it; R or pad Start restart a finished build. Cabinet class DesktopGames/DaedalusDesktopStonecourseCore.h, registry id stonecourse, save slot stonecourse.dgs.

items.text: A dressed wall stone one, two or three cells wide; grey blocks on the wall, teal once their course locks.
The supply cart showing the next six stones.
The levelled trench the first course sits on; it supports any stone.
Where skipped stones go; three skips a build.
The gold bar under the wall where the next stone's left edge sits, and the ghost stone above it.

storyline.text: The boundary wall of the Prismheart yard came down in the thaw; the cart is loaded and the mason has left you the string line.
Three rows on the first stone: a column sets the stone on the lowest course that holds it fully, a gapless course locks, skips send a stone to the rubble. (They leave after the first stone.)
Each difficulty is a wider, taller wall with a longer supply to read ahead through: 7 x 4 with 20 stones, 8 x 5 with 26, 9 x 6 with 34.
The last course locks and the wall stands; every stone left on the cart and every skip unused is the mason's thanks.
The supply runs out with a course open, or a stone fits nowhere with the rubble pile full. Pad A or R draws the same supply again so the gaps can be planned.
The wall yard sits at the far end of the Prismheart arcade row after the weigh-house; a side craft, not a campaign gate, and locked courses add to the arcade scoreboard.
